title: Login splash, post-login routing and the legacy VK return
why: `meAuthRoute` picks where a user lands after login. On its own it handles two cases: the CRM screen when `__meBootCrm` is set (maya-os-site/index.html L38231), and the client cabinet when the fresh-login flag is set (L38228-38230). The third destination — apply identity, refresh `/me`, pick the workspace from the server-issued tenant bundle — is run by a second copy of the same logic inside MEApp's own initial state (L35660-35691). That split is the defect these rows record: "where does this role land" is implemented twice and divergently, and each copy handles cases the other does not. This is not a navigation-inventory group — all three rows are marked as not primary-nav — so what collapses here is the landing root, not menu entries. Because chat-first changes the default destination for every role, this resolver is the single place that change can be made safely, which makes this group a precondition for the 101 → 5 primary-nav collapse, not a consequence of it.
disappear: One of the two divergent role-to-destination resolvers, and role-keyed screen selection itself — the proposed successor resumes the conversation instead of choosing a screen. The legacy VK `?code` return on `app-tenant.html` (L23166-23172) also goes; VK surfaces are forbidden by the project's own rule (CLAUDE.md, gotcha 7). But it goes only once the Yandex return path exists on that bundle: deleting the VK half without adding the Yandex half makes this bundle worse, not cleaner. The splash does not disappear as a behaviour — it is a render state of the login screen (`lgSplash` L6340, early return L8195), folded in as an optional first paint, and its row requires that both of its behaviours survive the merge, neither silently dropped. Nothing here removes the promo or trial slide-to-unlock gift: those are separate rows (S-076, S-108, S-146, S-283), moved into chat widgets or kept as a capability. All three rows in this group are retire-after-parity (K16) — nothing is removed before the merged surface proves it does the same job.
remain: Authentication itself — and the merge target is still unnamed. On all three rows the successor reads "to be named, requires signature", so "one `auth` capability" is a proposal for the owner to approve, not a finding the evidence already supports. The fresh-login signal and workspace selection stay: apply identity, refresh `/me`, pick the workspace from the server-issued tenant bundle. What goes is the automatic screen jump, not the signal. `lgSplash`'s second job stays too: it currently gates four login effects (L6389, L6738, L6740, L6753), and the successor must keep that scheduling or move it somewhere explicit. On `app-tenant.html` a working social-login return must remain, which means ADDING `__meMaybeYandexNativeReturn` / `handleYandexRedirect` — as `app.html` already carries at L41575-41576 — not merely deleting VK. And the resolver stays what the evidence calls it, an authority-to-destination resolver: it decides where a user lands, never what that user may do. The successor must not turn a landing into a permission.
risk: MEDIUM — unchanged, and bounded by the rows' own condition: all three are retire-after-parity (K16), so nothing is deleted until the merged surface proves parity. Three hazards must be carried into that parity check. (1) `app-tenant.html` has no Yandex return handler today, so a Yandex callback landing on that bundle is already unhandled; the merge must ADD that path rather than merely delete the VK branch, or the bundle is left with no working social return at all — and the row notes the same `web_session_token` gap applies here as to the app.html VK path. (2) Collapsing to whichever of the two resolvers looks simpler drops the other's cases and produces role-dependent, intermittently wrong landings — and landing a user in the wrong workspace is exactly the tenant confusion the authorization forbids ("Никогда не угадывать tenant для effectful action"). (3) Removing `lgSplash` naively fires the email-sheet focus and keyboard effects on first paint. One mismatch deserves the owner's eye: the login-splash row's evidence-derived owner is `onboarding`, while the group is proposed under `auth · routing`. The frozen limitations are untouched — this group changes where a user lands, not what is enforced.
user_impact: Who notices depends on auth state and bundle, not on role. **The splash is a logged-out surface, not a universal one.** The white MAYA logo screen (S-003 — `MayaSplash`, app.html L15870: 2300 ms hold + 300 ms fade, 700 ms under prefers-reduced-motion, tap anywhere to skip, once per browser session via sessionStorage `me_maya_mark_splash`) is a render state of ALogin (`lgSplash` L6340, early return L8195). MEApp's initial screen resolves from the stored `me_saas_auth_v2:<ns>` bundle straight to home / staff-home / panel / god / access-compat (L38578-38640), so a signed-in user never mounts ALogin and never sees it; a legacy Telegram-token user does start at `login`, but meAuthRoute's boot poll routes them away in ~50-100 ms (L41582), so they see a flash, not 2.3 s. It is also app.html-only: app-tenant.html has no splash at all (0 hits for `lgSplash`/`MayaSplash`), and maya-os-site/index.html has a *different* one — 3200 ms, aurora backdrop, its own tap-to-skip (L5399-5415, L6871) — which belongs to S-073, not to this group, and survives this merge. Note also that S-003's row name («splash slide-to-unlock») conflates two separate things inside ALogin: the splash has no slide gesture, and the nearest real slide-to-unlock there is the trial-activation knob (`lgKnob` L6782, S-283 — KEEP AS CAPABILITY, with the exactly-once `lgTrialReq` guard), which must not be swept into this group by that wording. **The landing change is real but not new everywhere.** After login users stop arriving at a role-picked screen — client home, the «Я клиент / Я сотрудник» chooser, staff-home / a business panel tab / god, or Integrations via `__meBootCrm` — and arrive in the chat thread instead. On maya-os-site a client already lands in Maya chat today by both the SaaS and the legacy path (`meSaasOpenMayaChat('client','home')`, L38251 / L38254 / L38274), and app.html's meAuthRoute carries a comment recording that client chat-landing was deliberately removed there (L41530-41531) — so for app.html clients this is the reversal of a recent product decision the owner should be told about, not a first-time gain. «Resume» is a K3/B21 deliverable, not today's behaviour: `meSaasOpenMayaChat` mints a fresh `__meChatVisitKey` on every open precisely so AChat remounts (index.html L4971), so the honest claim is "lands in the chat thread", with resume as the thing the successor must add. The chooser is not simply deleted either — the group's own WHAT WILL REMAIN keeps workspace selection, and the chooser is reached exactly when the workspace is ambiguous (`meSaasEffectiveWorkspace` empty / `resolved.chooser`), which is the case the conditional approval requires the successor to ask about. **On the tenant bundle a client can lose their only way in.** «Войти через VK ID» is rendered and wired there (app-tenant.html L4026 → `loginVk` L22812); that bundle has no email login (`lgEmail` 0 hits) and no Yandex handler in boot (only `handleVkRedirect`, L23170), so S-614 leaves Telegram as the sole working login unless the merge adds Yandex as the row demands. For a VK-only client that is lost access, not a cosmetic change: no one's *permissions* change, but one population's ability to authenticate at all does.
security_impact: Neutral on server authorization, with one risk the group itself rates MEDIUM and two carry-overs — not "mostly neutral" flat. The role meAuthRoute reads is cached: `app_access` on the server-issued user inside the `me_saas_auth_v2:<ns>` bundle, plus the client-written `me_is_staff` flag on the legacy path. It only picks a destination — `meAppAccessFetchAndRoute` / `panel_me` re-decide immediately and the server validates every token — so collapsing the routing table removes no authorization gate. **Carry-over 1, verified unique.** `__meDropForeignLogin()` has exactly one caller in all three bundles, the first line of `meAuthRoute` (index.html L38222, app.html L41489, app-tenant.html L23122); it is published on `window` but nothing else calls it, and nothing else anywhere compares `Telegram.WebApp.initDataUnsafe.user.id` against stored `tg_auth_data` (app.html has only two other `initDataUnsafe` hits, both avatar code). It is therefore the only code that drops a previous Telegram user's `tg_auth_data` + `web_session_token` when a different Telegram account opens the same Mini App webview (app.html L41368-41382) — and only inside Telegram, since it returns early without a live `initDataUnsafe.user`, so the exposure is a shared Telegram webview/device, not any shared browser. The server cannot replace it because it never sees the initDataUnsafe mismatch, so a resume path that does not call it leaves a prior user's still-valid legacy session live and sendable as a credential. **Carry-over 2, duplicated but still required.** The same SaaS branch of meAuthRoute is also the fail-closed entry (`meAppAccessEnterCompat` / `__meGo('access-compat')` when `app_access` cannot be resolved, L41511-41512), the place a 401 from /me clears the stored session (`meSaasClearStoredSession('me_unauthorized')`, L41516-41517), and the place the stored bundle is scoped to the loaded tenant (L41505 — which accepts a bundle carrying no `tenant_slug` for any slug, a weakness to fix rather than copy). These also exist in MEApp's copy (L38590, L38784-38785) and the fetch wrapper (L12241/12252/12268), so no single one is unique — but the stated point of this group is to collapse to one resolver, so whichever resolver survives must keep all three. The residual risk is the one the group already names and this field omitted: a resume that guesses a workspace or tenant lands a user in the wrong one, which the authority model forbids for effectful action. Dropping the VK `?code` return removes one of three writers into `web_session_token` in app.html (VK L40891, Yandex L40957, applogin poll L41220) and one of two in app-tenant (L22852, L22985) — a store that «Выйти на всех устройствах» does not clear (`revokeAllMySessions` → DELETE /auth/sessions → `saasLogout` → `saasForceLogout` → `saasClearSession` never touches it; only `__meLogout` L41567 does; S-604, S-605, S-578) — and it does not close that gap, because the Yandex path S-614 requires writes the same store.
